course.title: Planetary Science
course.description: Examines planetary system formation, geophysics, atmospheres, climate evolution, magnetic fields, impacts, rings, satellites, exoplanet comparisons, and the chemical and physical conditions that shape planetary environments.

status.reviewStatus: Approved for review release; not yet approved for instructional use

cadence.rationale: Matched 1:1 biweekly cadence (each lab/problem-set pair follows a two-lecture block), following the ASTR230/ASTR310 precedent, confirmed against the actual lecture content rather than assumed from file counts. The course's six thematic units are of variable length (2-3 lectures each), but the lab/problem-set cadence remains a strict two-lecture grid throughout, so Lab/PS 05 deliberately spans the Unit 4 (Atmospheres)/Unit 5 (Fields and Giants) thematic boundary. See syllabus.html Lecture, Lab, and Problem-Set Cadence.

dataProvenance.src: materials/ASTR320/src/generate_astr320_content.py and generate_astr320_labs_psets.py generate all worked examples, lecture slides/notes, labs, and problem sets programmatically from shared constants.
realData: TRAPPIST-1 system (star and seven planets b-h) - live-verified via direct web fetch this session (Wikipedia "TRAPPIST-1", citing Agol et al. 2021, PSJ 2, 1; Ducrot et al. 2020, A&A 640, A112; Delrez et al. 2022, A&A 667, A59). Used in Lecture 14, Lab 07, PS 07.
Eight solar-system planets' mass/radius/orbit/albedo/temperature - standard published JPL Planetary Fact Sheet values, not independently re-verified this session - flagged for spot-check.

Io, Europa, Enceladus, Moon, Ceres, Vesta, Titan physical/orbital parameters - standard published solar-system literature values (Dawn, Cassini-Huygens missions), not independently re-verified this session - flagged for spot-check.
Moment of inertia factors (Earth, Mars, Moon, Mercury) and Mars/Earth heat-flow values - standard published geophysical values, not independently re-verified this session - flagged for spot-check.
Lunar crater-chronology calibration values - standard published values consistent with Neukum et al. 2001 / Stoffler & Ryder 2001, not independently re-verified this session - flagged for spot-check.

Jupiter/Earth/Uranus/Neptune magnetic field strengths and Uranus ring radii - standard published values (Connerney et al. 2018; Ness et al. 1986; Elliot et al. 1977), not independently re-verified this session - flagged for spot-check.
